subject: Next steps — TTFT warmstart thresholds & steady-stream cadence
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>

Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap: TTFT warmstart thresholds & steady-stream cadence

Hi Asha — thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap from our side and concrete next steps so we keep momentum.

Key performance targets you mentioned:
- User-facing TTFT target: 150 ms p95 for short prompts (<= 64 tokens).
- Acceptable range for longer prompts: p95 TTFT up to 300 ms (up to 512 tokens).
- Peak concurrent sessions estimate: 2k active websockets; average sustained throughput ~120 reqs/s.

Streaming requirements we discussed:
- Prefer SSE for the initial rollout (browser clients + mobile fallbacks).
- Chunk cadence: sub-second incremental chunks (we recommend 80–150 ms pacing) for perceived responsiveness while avoiding excessive small-tok overhead.
- Heartbeat/keepalive: 15s heartbeat to prevent idle connection drops behind proxies.

Warmstart vs cold-start notes:
- Your infra constraint: ~10% of sessions may hit a cold replica during spikes. We discussed warmstart priming to keep key model idle-buckets warm; estimated cost delta ~6–9% at projected load.

Action items:
1) I attached a concise probe plan (ttft-warmstart-probe-plan.xlsx) that outlines three lab probes: cold-start baseline, warmstart steady-state, and burst concurrency stress. Can you/your ops team confirm they can run the first two probes next week?
2) Please share the exact origin URLs and any reverse-proxy timeouts so we can tune heartbeat recommendations.
3) Kimberly, Ben — please add recommended config knobs (batch size / max-concurrency / kv-cache warmup) and an ops checklist for pilot.

If those dates work for you, I’ll lock in an intro call between Productly ops and our infra engineer (Ben) to walk the probe steps.

Thanks —Jonas

--

Nice call — adding a few practical guardrails from pricing and ops impact perspective: 

- Warm pool sizing: for your 2k concurrent sessions target we recommend a warm pool sized for ~8% of peak concurrency (so ~160 vCPU-backed replicas / or equivalent GPU warm slots depending on model footprint). That aligns with the 6–9% cost delta Jonas estimated.
- Autoscale policy: configure a short, aggressive scale-up (60s) and a more conservative scale-down (5–10m) to avoid oscillation.
- Batching: keep per-device batch_max around 16–32 for low-latency models; enable dynamic batching with a max_wait of 60 ms.
- KV cache priming: pre-warm caches with a synthetic priming set from typical system prompts (we can provide a small set).

Ben — can you draft the pilot runbook steps (probe sequence, telemetry collection fields, p95/p99 comparisons) and share by EOD so Productly can review before Tue?

Thanks — I’ll have the pilot runbook back to the thread by COB today. High-level plan:

0) Pre-checks: confirm origin URLs, proxy timeouts, client sample rates.
1) Cold baseline (10m window): measure cold TTFT distribution, CPU/GPU spin-up latencies.
2) Warmstart steady-state (20m): start with warm pool at 8% concurrency, measure p50/p95/p99.
3) Burst stress (5m bursts): inject 3x expected traffic to validate autoscale policy and failover fallback to smaller quantized model.
4) Telemetry fields: ttft_ms, chunk_interval_ms, first_chunk_bytes, total_tokens, backend_qps, active_conns, replication_warm_count.
